title: The minimal primes of the strict henselization of a tensor product of strictly henselian local algebras correspond to pairs of minimal primes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an algebraically closed field k and strictly henselian local k-algebras A and B with residue field k, forms the strict henselization C of A tensor_k B at the maximal ideal m_A tensor_k B + A tensor_k m_B, and asserts that the minimal primes of C correspond one-to-one to pairs of minimal primes of A and B (source lines 31855-31863). The proof reduces the correspondence to a uniqueness statement. It first observes that a minimal prime r of C maps to minimal primes p of A and q of B because the ring maps A -> C and B -> C are flat, using going down for flat maps (proof lines 31866-31871). It then notes that it suffices to show the strict henselization of (A/p tensor_k B/q) at the corresponding maximal ideal has a unique minimal prime, and that A/p and B/q are again strictly henselian, so one may assume A and B are strictly henselian local domains and prove that C has a unique minimal prime (proof lines 31872-31881). The substantive step is the use of geometric unibranchness: the integral closures A' and B' of A and B in their fraction fields are normal local domains with residue field k, so that A' tensor_k B' is normal, hence its localization R at the corresponding maximal ideal is a normal local domain (proof lines 31882-31894). The proof then shows that A tensor_k B -> A' tensor_k B' is integral and that the maximal ideal of A' tensor_k B' over the given one is unique, so the displayed localization R can be rewritten with the smaller maximal ideal, and concludes that the localization of A tensor_k B is integrally closed in R, so R is its integral closure (proof lines 31895-31909). Applying geometric unibranchness once more gives that C has a unique minimal prime, completing the proof (proof lines 31910-31913). The non-routine content is the two-fold use of geometric unibranchness together with the normality of the tensor product of the integral closures.
